title: Evening Classes at a Community Centre

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Hello, Ashgrove Community Centre, Siobhan speaking.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Hi there. I picked up your autumn brochure, but it's a bit out of date, I think, and I wanted to check some details about the evening classes.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Yes, sorry about that. A few things have changed since it was printed. Which classes are you interested in?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Three, possibly. Pottery, Spanish and photography. Let's start with pottery. It's on Mondays, right?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: That's right, Monday evenings from seven. It used to be held in Room 9, but we've had a new kiln put in, so it's moved to Room 14, at the back of the building.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Room 14. And the brochure says it's eighty pounds?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: That was last year's price, I'm afraid. It's now ninety-five pounds for the eight weeks, but that includes all the clay and the firing.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: OK. Do I need to bring anything?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Tools are provided, but it does get messy. The tutor asks everyone to bring an apron. Old clothes are fine too, but an apron is the main thing.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Got it. Now, Spanish. The brochure has it on Tuesday nights.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Ah, that's one of the changes. The tutor couldn't do Tuesdays this term, so it's on Wednesday now. Same time, half past six, in the library upstairs.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Wednesday. That actually suits me better. Is it sixty pounds?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Yes, sixty is correct for Spanish.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: And what level is it? I did a little at school, but honestly I've forgotten nearly everything.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: We had an intermediate group last year, but there weren't enough people this time, so this term it's only for beginners. It sounds like that would suit you.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Perfect. And finally, photography.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Photography is Thursday, in the main hall. The price has gone up a bit because we've added two trips, one to the coast and one to the botanical gardens. It's now a hundred and twenty pounds, including the coach. Not a hundred and ten as it says in the brochure.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: That still sounds like good value. Is there any kind of discount available? I'm doing more than one class.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: We don't do a discount for multiple classes, unfortunately. We used to give ten per cent off for that, but it stopped last year. What we do have is a discount for anyone who lives in the town. That's fifteen per cent off every class.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Oh, I live on Mill Street, so that should be fine. Fifteen per cent, great.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Lovely. Is there anything else I can help with?

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Yes, parking. Is there a car park at the centre?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: There is, but it's pay and display, and it fills up quickly in the evenings. Most of our students leave their cars at the supermarket across the road. It's free after six, and it's only a two-minute walk.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Great tip. And how do I enrol? Can I do it online?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: You can fill in the form online, but you do need to come in once before the course starts so we can check you're a local resident for the discount. Just bring proof of address, like a council tax letter. You don't need a photo or anything like that.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: Proof of address. Fine. And the brochure mentioned an open evening where you can meet the tutors?

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Yes, that's moved as well, I'm afraid. It was going to be on the second of September, but the hall is being painted that week. It's now on the fourth of September, from six until eight.

script.speaker: Caller
script.text: The fourth. I'll put it in my diary. Thanks, Siobhan, you've been really helpful.

script.speaker: Officer
script.text: Not at all. We'll see you on the fourth, then.
